Valhalla's Tide Bestiary

Every creature and enemy ship in the game: 45 kinds in 13 families (one of them friendly), plus 6 ships, and now (v0.8.7) every game mechanic at the end, each with its own notes box. Each one has a picture in the sea (how you meet it) and a full-body picture with the sea taken away, so you can judge the whole model.

Write what you would change in any box and tap Needs a redesign to flag it. There is a box for each kind and one for each whole family (use that for changes to the shared body, like the eel's neck).

Level. The name tag shows Lv. Its colour compares it with your ship: green weaker, white even, orange stronger, red much stronger, purple deadly.
Hull and Hits are its health and one hit before your shields. Monsters come from about one level below your ship to nearly two above, so Meets ships says which ship sizes run into it.
Chasing. A stronger monster chases at 86% of your top speed and gives up after 24 seconds. Touching one starts a battle where it strikes first; tap FIGHT to strike first yourself.

Overall

Sharks

4 kinds
  • Fast hunters that cruise just under the surface, so mostly you see the dorsal fin; they leap clear of the water to bite.
  • Jaws-style heads: a pointed snout overhangs a mouth of triangular teeth, and when one bites the snout lifts and the jaw thrusts forward.
  • A shark can take your bait while you fish: a bite starts a battle on the spot.
  • Most common in Home Waters and the Warm Sea.
  • Speed 10.5 (your ships sail at 9 to 13).
  • In battle it lunges from the right, lunges from the left or leaps to bite.

Legends

3 bosses
  • They never appear at random. Each sleeps in its lair, marked on the map, and rises when you sail in with a big enough ship.
  • Slay all three for the LORD OF THE SEA ending.

The Kraken

Kraken's Maw, far north-east · needs a Snekkja
  • A true giant: each eye is about as long as a Snekkja. It lies mostly underwater with tentacles thicker than your hull rising all around you, and in battle the camera looks past your ship at one great eye. Sleeps at its lair until you sail in with a Snekkja or bigger.
  • Speed 6. Attacks three times a turn: sweeps a tentacle from the right, sweeps a tentacle from the left or drags at the hull.

Ships at sea

6 kinds
  • Raider longships come in every ship size (a raider's level is its size). They shoot four-arrow volleys from 12 to 34 away, then fight a ship battle. Half again as common in the Mist Sea.
  • Raider fleets (a sea event) bring two to four ships of one clan, led by a Warlord one size bigger. Sink them all for their war chest.
  • Winning a ship battle pays timber, iron and gold.

Treasure Knarr

Your level

Golden sail with a coin, chests with glowing gold lids, no weapons. A sea event: it runs from you at 80% of your top speed and throws cargo overboard as you close in. Catch it to board her (you strike first, it hits weakly) for triple gold.

Game mechanics

44 mechanics (v0.8.7)
  • Everything the game does, as it stands now: sailing, the world, fighting, harbours and the ship, fishing and treasure, Helheim, saving. Each has a notes box and a Needs a change flag, like the monsters.
  • Numbers are the game's own (ship sizes, levels, percentages), so a note can say what should move and by how much.

Sailing and controls

6 mechanics

The helm and telegraph

The half-wheel steers and stays where you leave it; a double tap centres it. The sail telegraph has five notches: BACK, STOP, ROW, HALF, FULL. On PC: A/D or arrows steer, W/S step the telegraph, Space throws a spear ahead, C changes the view, E opens the chart, F does the round button's job.

One-handed layout: every button sits on one side; the ⇄ button swaps sides for left-handed play.

Views

CHASE (behind the ship, zoomed out), HELM (at the wheel, the eye moved back and up) and FAR. Battles lift the action up the screen and zoom in; fog thins in a fight.

The sea chart and courses

The corner minimap and the full chart (pinch to zoom) are the same map. Tap anywhere to set a course: the ship steers to the ✕ and stops; pulling the telegraph back cancels it. SAIL TO DOCK plans a route round the land and flees every fight on the way.

The chart marks harbours ⚓, lairs, your wreck ☠, treasure ✕, Hel's Gate 🌀, the maelstrom and the aurora.

Compass and sunstone

Compass I shows your heading. Compass II (the sunstone) also points to the nearest harbour, your nearest treasure map, your wreck, and Hel's Gate until you have crossed it.

Speed, turning and the sea

Top speed = the ship's speed × (1 + 10% a Sail level, 5% past V) × boosts (porpoises 10%, Bifröst 25%, Thor's Fury and the escape row 35%) × design perks. Oars & Crew add turning and acceleration. Storms slow you; big waves pitch and roll the hull; the water never clips through the deck.

Land, rocks and running aground

Islands, rocks, bergs, reefs and the map edge are solid: the hull slides along them and stops. Leaving a harbour puts you on the most open heading clear of land.

The world

7 mechanics

The five seas of Midgard

Home Waters, the Frost Sea (ice, bergs, the aurora), the Storm Sea (lightning, waterspouts), the Mist Sea (fog, the ghost ship, Hel's Gate) and the Warm Sea (reefs, corals). Each sea changes which monsters appear and has its own song; a banner names it as you cross in.

Monsters scale with your ship

No fixed-level zones: every spawn is levelled from your ship size (−1 to +1.5 levels, most at your level). A beast 1.5+ levels above its own kind is "Dread" and a little bigger. Raiders come in sizes around yours. A stronger monster chases at 86% of your top speed and gives up after 24 s; a beast you shoot sprints after you for 3.5 s.

Day and night

A full day lasts a few minutes. At night more monsters spawn (anglers, megalodons, the ghost ship), monsters see you later, and the lanterns add fishing spots.

Weather

Clear, rain, storm, fog, snow in the Frost Sea, ash in Helheim. Storms bring big waves and lightning: a bolt that strikes your mast gives Thor's Fury (double damage, +30% defence) for 20 s. Rogue waves and tornadoes lift and fling the ship.

Sea events

Every 1 to 2 minutes at sea: a maelstrom 🌀 (full sail to escape its pull), a serpent ambush, a raider fleet (3 to 4 ships that hunt you; break it for a war chest), a treasure knarr (runs at 80% of your speed and throws cargo; catch and board her), or the aurora in the Frost Sea at night (sail into the Bifröst pillar: hull mends, +25% speed for 30 s).

Porpoises

A friendly pod now and then; while two or more ride your bow wave you sail 10% faster.

Fishing spots, flotsam and treasure spots

Bubbling spots near the ship: fish (the fishing mini-game), flotsam (free timber, iron or gold) or a gold treasure spot. Lanterns add spots at night and make more of them treasure.

Fighting

12 mechanics

Classic monster fight (turn-based)

You fire three shots a volley on a moving aim bar: the weak spot (bigger with each Ballista level) does more. Then the monster attacks: DODGE left or right, or BRACE ⬆ for an overhead attack, within the timer. Higher levels give less time and two attacks a round; legends three. FLEE costs a hit and stuns it. Thor's Fury doubles your damage and widens the windows.

Fire pots

A fire pot replaces one of the volley's three shots for a big burning hit (2.2× to 3.6× by level); one pot a volley, 1 + level/2 pots a battle.

Special moves

In a round's first attack an octopus may wrap its arms round your hull and a serpent or leviathan coil round the ship: hack at it 5 to 10 times in 2.8 s (tap, Space, any dodge key) to break free, or it drags you under for 1.4× a hit. In Helheim burning crabs and eels set the deck ablaze (douse it) and undead sharks, megalodons and anglers feed on you (drive them off, or they heal by what they took).

Action ship battle (the battle line)

Ship fights form a battle line: you and the enemy ships sail along parallel lanes. Fire when a ship crosses your reckoning; a perfect crossing does 1.6×. She aims for 0.8 s before each volley: change speed on the telegraph during her aim and most of her volleys fall wide. Fleet ships join the line (up to four). Near land with no room for a line the fight goes classic ("close quarters"). The pause menu switches ACTION BATTLES on or off.

Boarding and prize ships

With grappling hooks of the right level you can BOARD a ship once her hull is under 40%: a crew fight. Win and choose PLUNDER (cargo) or CLAIM her: she waits at a mooring (3, or 4 with the Jarl's Hall) and you can SAIL HER (she keeps her own colours and no design perks) or SELL her.

Spears and the ballista at sea

Outside a fight, FIRE throws a spear (or a ballista bolt) at the nearest monster ahead, with a reload of 1.2 s (ballista 0.95 to 0.8 s). It hurts and enrages ordinary beasts; legends shrug it off outside their fight.

The iron ram

Hitting a monster head-on above half speed rams it for free damage (up to 60% of its hull), more with each Ram level.

Damage and defence

Your hull = 100 × 1.75 a ship size × (1 + 25% an Iron Plates level) × perks. A monster's hit = 9 × 1.5 a level (1.75 past level 4), reduced by your defence: shields and plates up to 70% (a little more past rune V), 85% with Thor's Fury. The draugr curse cuts defence by 20% for 60 s unless the Elder sign sail is fitted.

Crew mending and repair

With Oars & Crew the hull mends at sea when nothing has hit you for a while (7% a minute at level I up to 60% at VIII). Harbours REPAIR for timber and gold.

Sinking and the wreck

At 0 hull you sink: VALHALLA CALLS, then you rise again at your home harbour with half your cargo; the rest waits in a wreck ☠ on the chart to salvage. Upgrades, souls and designs are never lost.

The legends (bosses)

Each sleeps in its lair and rises for a ship big enough; in a smaller ship only its young rise, or sometimes the legend itself (FLEE!). The Kraken: cut the tentacles that grab you, shoot its eye. Jormungandr: it stalks under the water; sail out of its red ring, then shoot its head. The Elder One: repeat its runes to break the ward, shoot the eye when it flashes if it lifts you. Helheim's three (Hafgufa, Surtr, Nidhögg) are the same fights grown dead and far stronger.

Lair waves, Reborn legends and trials

Staying in a lair brings waves of its young, each stronger. A slain legend can rise again as "Reborn" from wave 2 for a ship a size bigger than it needs (+½ level and +25% souls each time, five times). Holding out to wave 5 and wave 10 pays a trial reward once.

Harbours and growing the ship

7 mechanics

The eight ships

Faering, Karvi, Snekkja, Skeid, Drakkar, then the great ships: Busse (needs Midgard's three legends slain), Ormen Lange (souls) and Naglfar (Helheim's three legends). Each is bigger, tougher (×1.75 hull) and hits harder (×1.65), and the seas grow with it. The next-ship card shows her real hull.

Upgrades and rune levels

Shield Wall, Iron Plates, Ballista, Fire Pots, Sail, Oars & Crew go to level VIII; Iron Ram III, Lanterns III, Compass II, Grappling Hooks IV, Nets IV. An upgrade can go one level past your ship size. Levels IV and up are rune levels; V to VIII need souls from Helheim, and each great ship opens one more (VI the Busse, VII the Ormen Lange, VIII the Naglfar).

The shipwright: hull and sail designs

34 designs, each with a small perk (speed, hull, turning, damage, defence, souls, gold, fishing, mending, how late monsters spot you). Some are bought with resources, some need a great ship and souls, some are dyed for gold alone, and each slain legend leaves one. Tap a design to preview it on your ship. NAME HER names the ship.

Timber, iron, gold, fish and souls

Kills pay gold and iron (ships timber too), fishing pays fish to sell, digs and spots pay gold. Souls 👻 come only from Helheim. The trader sells iron and timber for gold; the Jarl's Hall (Valholm or Gjallarhöfn) is a gold sink with five stages of perks; Hel's tithe buys +25% souls for 10 minutes.

Bounties

Every harbour posts one bounty: slay N of a kind, sink or take N ships, hunt in a sea, fish N spots, break a fleet, slay a legend's young. Take one at a time; CLAIM it at any harbour; DROP leaves it posted where it came from. They count only in their own realm.

The Jarl's saga

Thirteen deeds with three or four ranks each (Monster Slayer, Shark Hunter, Ship Breaker, Fisher, Treasure Hunter, Bounty Hunter, Legend Slayer, Soul Reaper, Bestiary, Master Shipwright, Lord of Ships…). Each rank pays gold (and souls once you have some) and the best deed gives the Jarl a title. Open it from the pause menu.

The Jarl's Hall

Five stages for 2k to 40k gold plus timber and iron: a fourth mooring, +2 gold a fish, 10% off upgrades and ships, crew mend +25%, +5% damage and hull.

Fishing, treasure and salvage

4 mechanics

Fishing

At a bubbling spot, FISH: keep the catch inside the moving box until the bar fills. Nets make the box bigger and the catch larger; Odin's raven sail adds 25%. Fish sell at harbour.

Treasure maps and digs

Sunk ships sometimes drop a map: a clue names an island and landmarks, the chart marks it ✕. LAND there and dig: a grid where nearby cells say warmer or colder; find the chest in the tries you have. Three maps a realm. Helheim digs pay souls. A relic map leads to Draugr's Bane.

Salvage and wrecks

Old wrecks on the chart can be salvaged for a one-time haul (they refill over time); your own wreck holds the cargo you lost when you sank.

The ghost ship and Draugr's Bane

A draugr ghost ship sails the Mist Sea and the night once you have a Snekkja. Boarding her leaves the curse (−20% defence for 60 s); sinking her drops a relic map to Draugr's Bane, which makes her crew's curse harmless.

Helheim

5 mechanics

Hel's Gate

Far west in the Mist Sea, a ring of rune stones round a swirling disc. A Drakkar or bigger can pass: a confirm screen, a purple fade, and you arrive beside the gate home at Gjallarhöfn. The 🌅 gate there takes you back. Crossing clears every chase.

The realm of the dead

Its own seas (Gjöll, Niflheim, Muspelheim, Náströnd, Ginnungagap), harbours and lairs; a burning sky by day and a purple swirling abyss by night; dead trees, bone reefs, soul lights, ash rain; its own dirge and fire-drum music.

The undead

Every monster and ship is an undead version with its own colours and name (Drowned, Burning, Rime-dead…), half a level stronger, with more hull (1.4× on a Drakkar, up to 2× on a Naglfar) and harder hits, and the special moves above. Draugr fleets, Hel's soul barge (throws soul orbs as it flees) and wandering soul orbs.

Souls

Every undead kill pays souls: 2 + 2 × (its level above your ship), ×1.5 for ships, ×2 for a legend's young, ×3 for the barge, × design perks and the tithe. Legends pay 150. Souls buy rune levels V to VIII, soul-priced designs, the Ormen Lange (250) and the Naglfar (300). Sinking never loses them.

Hel's armada

Once Helheim's three legends are slain and you sail a Naglfar there, a fleet of six led by Hel's Admiral rises every 17 to 23 minutes, a level stronger than a fleet, for three times the war chest and 60 souls more.

Saving and settings

3 mechanics

Saving

The game autosaves at sea and in harbour; CONTINUE VOYAGE shows your ship and realm. SAVE CODE on the title gives a code to carry the voyage to another device. NEW VOYAGE needs a second tap (it deletes the save). SAVE & QUIT waits until a fight is over.

Sound, music, battles, side

SOUND and MUSIC switch separately (keep the game sounds, play your own music). ACTION BATTLES ON / OFF in the pause menu. ⇄ swaps the control side. FULL SCREEN on the title. Add to Home Screen plays it as an app.

The tutorial and HOW TO PLAY

A short tutorial card walks a new voyage through the wheel, the telegraph, docking and the first fight; HOW TO PLAY on the title holds the full rules.

Pictures captured from the game's showcase page. Levels, hull and hits follow the game's formulas (hull 45 × 1.65 per level, a hit 9 × 1.5 per level; legends at 80% hull).
